title: Six Legs and a Table: The Stewart Platform, Easy One Way and Iterative the Other, and Where Its Legs Lose Their Grip

questions.question: For a parallel platform, which direction of kinematics has a formula?
options: Pose from leg lengths, as for a serial arm
Both, since the platform is rigid
Neither: both need an iteration
Leg lengths from a pose
questions.explanation: Give the pose and each leg is the distance between two known points. Going from lengths to a pose is the hard direction, the reverse of a serial arm.

questions.question: At home the legs were all:
options: 0.300 m, the height of the platform
questions.explanation: The layout is symmetric, so with the platform level and centred every leg is the same. 0.366 to 0.410 m was the range a raise and a tilt needed.

questions.question: How is the pose found from the lengths?
options: By the formula used the other way round
By trying every pose on a grid
By Newton's iteration from a guess
By trilateration, as for the delta
questions.explanation: There is no simple formula. From a guess the lengths' sensitivity to the pose gives a correction, and four rounds of that found the pose.

questions.question: What limits a platform's reach?
options: The torque of the motors
Leg stroke (and joint cones, not modelled)
The radius of the base
The number of legs
questions.explanation: A raise of 50 mm and a tilt of 10 degrees already needed legs from 0.366 to 0.410 m. Run out of stroke and the pose cannot be had.

questions.question: What is dangerous about a parallel singularity?
options: The legs need an infinite speed there
The pose can no longer be computed
The platform locks and cannot be moved
The platform can give way under a load
questions.explanation: A serial arm at a singularity cannot move in some direction. A parallel platform at one can move with its legs fixed, so it cannot hold a force that way.

questions.question: What is a good starting guess in a controller?
options: The home pose, every time
The last pose
A pose chosen at random
The middle of the legs' stroke
questions.explanation: The platform has barely moved since the last cycle, so the last pose is already close and a few steps finish it.
